parsed.explanation: Combined regime has no capital or presentation offence, but operative birth-sex rules create tier-1 exposure: federal and many subnational facility bans, document discrepancies at entry risking refusal and a fraud-based permanent-ineligibility inquiry, and birth-sex custody documented with sexual assault and dismissed failure-to-protect claims. Courts, injunctions, national hate-crime and housing/employment enforcement provide partial recourse, and no police sweeps or extortion campaign is documented. That places it below reduced-risk levels despite functioning litigation, and above severe targeting levels.

entry_documents.exposure: X markers stopped for new passports though existing X passports remain valid; reported confiscations/blocking. Entry cable requires refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation, though never automatic.
entry_documents.protection: Litigation by civil-liberties union and several executive orders blocked or enjoined; existing X passports valid until expiration.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate from entry questioning to refusal/fraud inquiry, then to detention and birth-sex placement; operative status depends on litigation at travel time.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National custody: conversion-therapy model, hormone removal, forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse reported. Division: trans woman housed with male prisoners, celled with convicted sex offender who assaulted her; court dismissed claims in 2022 as de minimis.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime and employment law exist, but no documented remedy changing the custody placements; 2017 gender-identity transfer guidelines were rescinded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Birth-sex placement follows the traveller after entry, facility-trespass arrest, or other detention; court dismissal in division corroborates lack of effective recourse for that placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. Maps: 9 units ban in all government buildings, 9 cover schools and some government buildings, 3 schools-only, 6 extend to some private settings; 4 make use criminal in certain circumstances. Division 2023 order backs single-sex bathrooms/changing rooms.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 units, 4 units and capital district have no mapped ban; private hotels may offer inclusive facilities. Division enforcement provision not documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal ban overlaps subnational bans; traveller cannot rely on a protective locality to override federal facilities or a ban in the division. Documented arrest under a trespass law elsewhere shows criminal exposure where enacted.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care under 19, upheld 6-1 in 2024; national proposed rules would bar public insurance for under-18 care. National custody reports hormone denial/removal.
care_services.protection: Not documented for trans-specific emergency ward placement or medication continuation for visitors.
care_services.interaction: Emergency or detained placement by birth sex can interrupt care; a parent cannot obtain banned care for a travelling minor in the division.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders frame sex as binary at birth, remove gender-identity policies, ban trans athletes, and counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; diversity framed as danger in facilities/sports policy. Public poll 66% supports assigned-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2020 Supreme Court ruling prohibits gender-identity employment discrimination; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity since 2009. Several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing by institutions raises outing and enforcement probability, but active litigation and injunctions show contested, not uncontested, state policy.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-19 care banned in division; June 2025 sports ban bars trans athletes; national order directs investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition including names/pronouns, though several orders are enjoined.
minors_guardians.protection: Marriage and adoption recognition for same-sex couples is settled nationally; no documented visitor shield for minor care or school participation.
minors_guardians.interaction: Adult travelling with a minor faces care denial and potential school/sports exclusion; a minor seeking care becomes subject to ban, not a protected traveller service.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented organised police sweeps, extortion, or trans-specific violence statistics for the division. Division hate-crime law does not cover gender identity; custody assault and national custody abuse are documented harms.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime coverage, housing enforcement from 2021, and municipal ordinances in one city since 2012 provide partial recourse; another city's ordinance was repealed in 2022.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of local gender-identity hate-crime coverage shifts recourse to national law; documented custody harm shows state response can fail where traveller is detained.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Facility, entry and custody remedies are litigated but unresolved; division facility-enforcement provision, current local marker practice, violence statistics, and stay-specific statutory position are not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have blocked/enjoined several orders and are hearing passport litigation, demonstrating functioning judicial recourse in principle.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty is not safety: traveller must verify operative federal and division rules at travel time, as exposure changes with injunctions and legislation.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this case on remedy and absence of targeting: no documented recurring police stops/extortion or near-universal facility exclusion with routinely rejected complaints as the operative local rule; functioning courts have enjoined orders. Shared tier-1 birth-sex facility/custody exposure keeps this well below 0.65.

Similar or slightly lower: both have birth-sex public-facility rules backed by removal/criminal trespass in some units and courts upholding key bans, with no organised arrests. This case adds entry fraud-ineligibility risk, national custody abuse reports, and threat framing, offset by X-passport validity and injunctions.

Higher than this case: 0.65-A has no universal facility ban, accepted nonbinary markers, working refunds and convictions. Here birth-sex facility/custody rules, document-discrepancy refusal risk, and dismissed custody-protection claims are documented operative exposures, not mere friction.

parsed.synthesis: Interaction: a passport/presentation discrepancy can trigger entry refusal or fraud inquiry, facility-trespass arrest where enacted, then birth-sex detention/ward placement with documented sexual-assault risk and weak recourse. Countervailing protections—existing X passports, national hate-crime/housing/employment enforcement, and active injunctions/litigation—prevent a high-risk rating but have not displaced the birth-sex facility, entry, custody, and minor-care rules. Adult alone faces facility/entry/custody exposure; adult with minor additionally faces care and sports bans.
